hints: Notice the question asks for the particle that has internal structure - recall which family contains the electron, neutrino and positron.
Connect each name to leptons versus hadrons - leptons are fundamental while hadrons are made of quarks.
Check the neutron for quark composition $udd$ and decide if something made of quarks can be fundamental.
walkthrough: Identify the four particles given: electron, neutrino, neutron and positron.
Recall the rule: fundamental particles in this syllabus are quarks and leptons, with no smaller constituents.
Recall that electrons, neutrinos and positrons are all leptons, so they are fundamental.
Recall that the neutron is a hadron, specifically a baryon made of three quarks with composition $udd$.
Conclude that because it is made of quarks, the neutron is composite and not fundamental. This is option C.

options.A: The electron is a lepton and is fundamental with no internal quark structure.
options.B: The neutrino is a lepton and is fundamental with no internal quark structure.
options.C: The neutron is a hadron made of three quarks, $udd$, so it is composite and not fundamental.
options.D: The positron is the antiparticle of the electron and is a fundamental lepton.
